_README: RUNTIME counterpart to golden.json. That file is a STATIC map (walk the
extracted cli.cjs for API references); this one records what the bundle
actually READ at run time, as reported by libexec/node-shim/internal/probe.cjs
under CLODE_SHIM_PROBE=1, while scripts/apicheck.mjs drives its corpus.
The two are complementary, and 2026-08-06 proved it: NEITHER of the session's
real defects appeared in the static map.
* fs/promises.statfs — reached through a minified alias (`cno.statfs`), which
defeated the static walker. The bundle CALLS it on its low-disk path, so
'undefined' became a bare 'not a function' (quickjs TypeErrors carry no
symbol name) swallowed by that path's own try/catch: the diagnostic simply
never appeared, and nothing failed.
* ChildProcess 'spawn' — an EVENT, not a property. Static API-surface
analysis cannot see events at all. Its absence made every stdio MCP server
unusable, silently.
A probe hit is BENIGN when the bundle only sniffs the property (typeof /
truthiness) and node also returns undefined. It is a BUG when the bundle goes
on to CALL it. Every entry must say which, and why.
Anything NOT listed here fails the gate. The point is that a new hit gets one
human look, not that this list is exhaustive. Add an entry only after checking
node's own answer for the same property.

benign.why: Electron detection. Electron sets process.type ('browser'/'renderer'); plain node leaves it undefined, which is what we return. Sniff only, never called.
NW.js detection. Defined only inside NW.js; undefined under node. Sniff only, never called.
The npm 'signal-exit' package's private singleton slot: it reads the key, finds it absent, and installs its own. Absence is the expected first-load state under node too.
